messages: Mia (Design): sharing a quick mock — we added a small 'dwell' badge next to the canary % to show how long it's been at X% (eg '5% · 2m'). thoughts? :eyes: Jordan (PM): love the intent. main Q: is the time always shown in minutes? can we surface 'elapsed vs target' somehow? eg '2m / 10m' so folks know when it will auto-promote. Mia (Design): good call — I tried both. '2m / 10m' gets a bit dense in the compact pill. we could expand on hover or when focused. Sam (Eng): from infra side, we already emit canary_start_ts + desired_window_sec. showing both is easy, hover expansion fine. keep default simple for mobile. Anya (Accessibility): accessibility nits: screen readers need clear phrasing — avoid 'dwell'. recommend aria-label readout like: 'Canary five percent, running two minutes of ten minute window'. Also ensure the badge is keyboard focusable so NVDA/VoiceOver users can hear expanded details. Mia (Design): +1 on avoiding jargon. I can switch microcopy from 'dwell' -> 'time in canary'. Would you be okay with '5% · 2m / 10m' visually and aria-label is the full sentence? Anya (Accessibility): yes. Also suggest an aria-live polite update when percent changes or when it finishes. small example: ``` Canary at 5 percent, 2 minutes of 10 completed ``` This will help screen reader users get automatic context without keyboard focus. Jordan (PM): we should be careful with too many live announcements — noisy dashboards can overwhelm. maybe only announce milestone events: start, hit threshold, promote, fail, rollback. Sam (Eng): agree. we can gate aria-live with logic: only announce on state transitions. also we already send event webhooks for milestones. Mia (Design): UI question — how to indicate an in-flight rollback option vs a completed rollback in the version timeline. current mock uses a red pill 'rolled back' that appears inline. but people said it's easy to miss. Jordan (PM): suggestion: add a subtle timeline marker with an icon + tooltip: 'Rollback to v3.2 initiated by @alex'. that gives context without pushing red everywhere. Sam (Eng): if we add icons, keep them semantic (use svgs with title attributes). also include a compact diff link in the tooltip so oncall can jump to what changed. Anya (Accessibility): tooltips need accessible triggers (focusable) and accessible names. Don't rely only on title attr — screen readers skip it. Provide visible tooltip on focus and aria-describedby to link to the tooltip content. Mia (Design): noted — I'll prototype focusable markers. Also debating copy for rollback CTA: 'Rollback to snapshot' vs 'Revert to previous'. Which is clearer? Jordan (PM): 'Revert to previous' is more user-friendly for product folks. 'Rollback to snapshot' is fine for infra-savvy teams. we support both flavors via settings? Mia (Design): maybe default to 'Revert to previous' and advanced dropdown 'Rollback options'. Sam (Eng): implementation caveat: 'revert' can be ambiguous when multiple previous versions exist. the action we implement will pick the last successful version. we should surface which version will be chosen in a confirmation modal. Mia (Design): yes, confirmation modal will show 'Reverting to v3.2 — would you like to proceed?' and keyboard-focused 'Cancel' primary to avoid accidental clicks. Anya (Accessibility): primary action being cancel is surprising for sighted users. Better pattern: put 'Cancel' as secondary and require Enter to confirm, but ensure focus is initially on Cancel? We need to be consistent with our existing modal patterns. If the team wants safer defaults, we can introduce an explicit 'Hold to confirm' or require typing the version string. Jordan (PM): let's not add friction for fast ops. confirmation modal + clearly labeled primary 'Revert to v3.2' + pattern that prevents accidental double-clicks (eg small delay) should be enough. Ops can enable stricter patterns in org settings. Mia (Design): OK — will keep standard modal, include keyboard trap and aria-describedby with the version diff link. Sam (Eng): small perf note: the timeline scrubber with many rollouts was lagging in the prototype — we need to virtualize list items and avoid heavy SVGs per row. Mia (Design): good call. I'll simplify per-row visuals and show full badges on hover to reduce DOM nodes. Jordan (PM): final ask: let's document the microcopy variants (compact vs expanded) and the SR readouts in the product PR so PM/Docs can review. Mia (Design): action items: 1) swap 'dwell' -> 'time in canary' text, 2) add 'elapsed / window' hover detail, 3) aria-live only for milestones, 4) accessible rollback marker + tooltip + confirm modal copy, 5) perf follow-up with eng. I'll push an updated mock later today. :thumbsup: deploy-bot: Deployment notice: canary rollout v3.5 started at 1739312000 by @sam — 5% target 10m window. Jordan (PM): perfect — thanks everyone, will sync in tomorrow's design review if anything changes.
